lead_story.topic: Arte Moreno sells Angels to Stan Kroenke for record $4B—longest playoff drought in MLB, Kroenke now owns Rams, Angels, Nuggets, Avalanche, Arsenal
lead_story.headline: Arte Moreno sells Angels to Stan Kroenke for record $4B—longest playoff drought in MLB, Kroenke now owns Rams, Angels, Nuggets, Arsenal

tweets.text:
The Los Angeles Angels are being sold to Rams owner Stan Kroenke and Kroenke Sports & Entertainment.

The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending MLB approval.

Kroenke also owns the Nuggets, Avalanche, Colorado Rapids, Colorado Mammoth and Arsenal Football Club.
Angels fans chant "goodbye Arte" after he sold the team

lead_story.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 2]: Reader knows Moreno is selling per yesterday's content. Today's new development: $4B sale price confirmed as MLB record (previous record was Cohen's Mets at $2.4B in 2020—nearly doubled), Kroenke Sports & Entertainment named as buyer, Angels fans chanted 'goodbye Arte' at ballpark Monday night. Skip the backstory about why Moreno is selling. Lead with the price, the portfolio Kroenke now owns (Rams won Super Bowl LXI in Feb 2027, Nuggets won 2025 NBA title, Arsenal finished 2nd in Premier League last year—this is a championship-winning ownership group), and the cruel irony: Moreno leaves with Angels having MLB's longest active playoff drought (11 years and counting), while Kroenke inherits a team that hasn't made the postseason since 2015 despite employing Mike Trout and Shohei Ohtani for most of that stretch. Historical comp: how does an 11-year drought rank among longest in MLB history? (Answer: it's tied for 12th all-time, but active longest by 3 years over the Marlins.) Also: Kroenke is only the second owner ever to control an NFL team + MLB team simultaneously (Jerry Reinsdorf owns Bulls/White Sox). What does his track record say about how he'll handle the Angels? Rams went from St. Louis to LA and got a $5B stadium and a Super Bowl—does he repeat the model in Anaheim or move them to a new market? Moreno bought the team for $184M in 2003 and sold it for $4B 24 years later—$3.816B profit, a 2,174% return. That's the second-best return in MLB history behind only John Henry's Red Sox (bought 2002 for $700M, now worth $6.7B = 857% gain, but Henry hasn't sold). Fan reaction angle: Angels fans are *celebrating* the sale because Moreno's reign included playoff failure, multiple failed big-name signings (Pujols, Hamilton, Rendon), and a decade of mediocrity. The 'goodbye Arte' chant is a sports rarity—fans cheering the sale of their team because they believe *anyone* would be better. Cross-sport comp: this is the Angels' version of the Commanders sale to Josh Harris—addition by subtraction.
lead_story.gif_concept: smug satisfaction after a long, exhausting ordeal finally ends

beats.angle: The sale price is a record and Kroenke's portfolio now looks like a fantasy sports monopoly
beats.landing: Reader grasps scale: Kroenke owns champions in three sports and just added a fourth franchise

beats.angle: The cruel irony: Moreno leaves with MLB's longest active playoff drought, and Kroenke inherits a team that wasted Trout and Ohtani
beats.landing: Reader feels the weight of 11 years of failure—rank it historically, name the comp droughts

beats.angle: Moreno turned $184M into $4B in 24 years, and fans are *celebrating* his exit
beats.landing: Reader hears the 'goodbye Arte' chant and understands: sometimes the best move an owner can make is selling

supporting_stories.headline: Tua Tagovailoa forgets to switch to burner account, comments on his own Instagram post: 'We're so proud of you!! You got this ❤️'

tweets.text:
Tua pulled a Kevin Durant and forgot to switch to his burner. 😭😭

 “We’re so proud of you!! You got this ❤️”

supporting_stories.research_notes: Tua commented on his own Instagram post Monday 'We're so proud of you!! You got this ❤️' without switching to burner account—pure Kevin Durant energy. HaterReport: 'His brain really is scrambled eggs 😭💀.' The internet immediately compared it to KD's famous burner account slip-up in 2017 when he forgot to log out of his main account before defending himself. HaterReport posted side-by-side of KD seeing Tua's mistake. LeBatardShow: 'It looks like Tua forgot to switch to the burner account 💔.' NFLMemes: 'Tua's fried brain forgot to switch to the burner account 😭', 'Tua ForgotToSwitchDaAccountOva.' This is a perfect storm: Tua has been the subject of concussion discourse for two years, he's entering a crucial season with the Dolphins, and now he's out here giving himself a pep talk on Instagram while pretending to be someone else. The joke writes itself. Research angle: how many athletes have been caught using burner accounts? (KD is the king, but Bryan Colangelo's burner scandal in 2018 was nuclear, and Eric Jr.'s dad ran burners defending Eric Jr. in the NFL.) What does the existence of burner accounts say about athlete psychology in the social media era? Also: Tua is coming off a 2025 season where he played 14 games, threw 28 TDs and 12 INTs, Dolphins went 9-8 and missed playoffs—this is not the time to be your own hype man in public.

The Taco Tuesday timing is *chef's kiss*. Research angle: Tacko's Celtics tenure was 2019-2021, and Jaylen was there for all of it. The win% stat is real (small sample size obviously), but it's a perfect encapsulation of how random NBA basketball can be. Also: what is the Sixers' actual plan here? Are they seriously rostering Tacko Fall, or is this a training camp body? If he makes the team, the Sixers' frontcourt is Joel Embiid, Tacko Fall, and... who else? This roster is *unserious* in the best way. Cross-sport comp: this is the NBA's version of the Manningcast signing Eli Manning as a backup QB—pure vibes, zero basketball logic.

supporting_stories.research_notes: Van Noy visited Vikings Monday per Schefter/Pelissero, signed Tuesday per Pelissero—will start on practice squad to ramp up. Won two Super Bowls with Flores when both were with Patriots per Pelissero. Now reuniting in Minnesota. Research angle: Van Noy is 35 years old, has played 12 NFL seasons, and just got cut by the Dolphins in August. He's a classic Patriots-era linebacker: versatile, smart, thrived in Belichick's system. Flores was the Patriots' linebackers coach from 2016-2018, then DC in 2019 before becoming Dolphins HC. Van Noy won Super Bowls LI (2017) and LIII (2019) with New England. Now Flores is the Vikings DC, and Van Noy is signing to the practice squad to ramp up—this is a reunion of two guys who know each other's systems inside and out. Cross-sport comp: this is the NFL's version of a veteran pitcher signing with his old pitching coach. The fit is perfect, the timing is right before Week 1, and the Vikings need linebacker depth. If Van Noy gets elevated to the 53-man roster, he's an immediate contributor.
